  - **When it doesn't:** if a story failed, was cancelled or stopped, or while planning is paused after research. The switch's row says why. Once the pause is lifted, it carries on if the switch is still on. An empty Next sprint starts nothing.
  - **Notice:** each automatic start shows a passive "Next sprint started: N stories" notification and is written to the debug log.
  - **Turning it off:** this never stops a sprint that's already running.

## Auto Start

Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept across reloads and restarts.
While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done, the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, or stopped never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why the next didn't start. Nor does the next start while planning is paused, as the paused section says: it starts once the pause is ended by Resume, or Approve, if the switch is still on. An empty Next sprint starts nothing.
Each time a sprint starts by itself, a passive notification says so, "Next sprint started: 4 stories", with a link that opens Planning, and the debug log records it. Turning the switch off never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from starting by itself.

## Saving

content.text:
Next sprint can now start on its own: Next sprint's heading has a "Start automatically" switch beside Send sprint. It's off by default and saved in `order.json`. A new test covering it passes, along with the existing planning, sprint, ribbon and card tests and clippy, all in a scratch copy of the project. I haven't tried it in the running app.

- **When it starts:** with the switch on, once every story in Current sprint has finished Done, the sprint closes and Next sprint is sent with no one pressing anything. With no sprint running, a story added to Next sprint starts it the same way.
- **When it waits:**
  - It never starts while planning is paused for research. Once Resume or Approve ends the pause it carries on, if the switch is still on.
  - It never starts after a sprint that ended with a failed, cancelled or stopped story. The switch's row then says why, in the warning colour.
  - An empty Next sprint starts nothing.
  - Turning the switch off never stops a sprint already running.
- **Notice:** each automatic start shows a passive "Next sprint started: N stories" notification with an "Open Planning" button, and is written to the debug log.

**Two choices of mine:**
- **Story being written:** it doesn't fire while you're writing a story in Next sprint. Otherwise a new, still-blank story would be sent the moment it appeared.
- **Empty stories stay behind:** stories with neither a title nor a prompt are never sent, by Send sprint or automatically. They stay in Next sprint. Before, an empty story could end up stuck in Current sprint and the sprint would never end.

**One limit:** the automatic start is checked when the plan changes or a task's status changes, but only for the project on screen. A project in the background won't start its next sprint until you switch back to it.
